claims.text: MLIPs trained on ab initio liquid-state configurations can serve as reference models for thermodynamic integration in multicomponent HEAs near melting.
Liquid-trained MLIP references will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to traditional EAM references.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch and free-energy errors.
The proposed intervention applies to HEAs containing 4–6 principal elements.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature.
The method is applicable where ab initio liquid snapshots can be generated at the relevant compositions and temperatures.
A liquid-trained MLIP captures diverse atomic environments and short-range order in the ab initio liquid.
Traditional EAM references do not adequately capture the diverse atomic environments and short-range order of the ab initio liquid.
MLIPs trained on liquid-state ab initio data encode many-body interactions and local structural diversity.
Encoding many-body interactions and local structural diversity increases overlap between MLIP-reference and ab initio-target phase spaces.
Increased phase-space overlap reduces mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
MLIP-referenced thermodynamic integration will yield free energies within 10–20 meV/atom of direct ab initio calculations.
MLIP references will reduce path mismatch and free-energy error by at least a factor of two relative to EAM references.
EAM references typically have larger discrepancies because they represent the liquid state poorly.
EAM potentials are known to represent ab initio liquid configurations in multicomponent alloys poorly.
Poor EAM representation of liquid configurations causes significant integration-path mismatch and free-energy errors.
The hypothesis may not apply to alloys with extreme chemical complexity or where MLIP training is infeasible.
The magnitude of improvement depends on MLIP quality and training-data diversity.
Residual mismatch may persist if the MLIP does not capture rare configurations.
